approach.method_basis: The Parent is a genetic algorithm that breeds molecular graphs from a population of up to sixty-four scored molecules. It draws parents from three high-ranking score bands, makes connected-fragment crossovers and local atom or bond edits, and sends each valid, novel offspring directly for evaluation. Accepted scores immediately update a greedy survivor population, so useful offspring can become parents of the next batch. This feedback loop worked, but most evaluated offspring scored below their generating parents.
approach.novelty: Add posterior-sampling selection before offspring reach the oracle. The same graph operators first generate a fresh pool; a fingerprint Gaussian process learned only from this task's accepted scores draws plausible score functions, and each batch position takes a different sampled function's best available offspring. This concentrates evaluations on promising generated structures while allowing uncertainty to change the choices. The lineage has only its root so far: no sibling has tested learned offspring selection, and the supplied mechanism-cluster history is empty. The new mechanism changes which generated offspring are evaluated; its training archive and diagnostics support that single selection mechanism.

hypothesis: Select oracle-bound offspring by maximizing independent joint posterior function draws from a task-local fingerprint Gaussian process over a fresh pool generated by the Parent's unchanged graph evolution operators.

finding_summary.headline: Posterior selection reproduces across seeds, but offspring yield stays below the historical parent-beating rate
finding_summary.insights: The experiment now separates reliable selector execution from the hoped-for improvement in offspring yield. The new runs' posterior means contain useful predictive information on the selected molecules: pooled prediction MSE is 0.017182 versus 0.036613 for the same-fit archive mean, with average within-batch rank correlation 0.412. Yet this information and widespread uncertainty-driven choice do not produce a higher parent-beating fraction. The remaining question is how to turn predictive information into more productive evaluations relative to already strong parents. Prediction quality is also uneven: on sitagliptin_mpo it is worse than the archive-mean predictor in two of three seeds, and that objective has the largest final-score variation. The chemistry assessment shows ample aromatic amides, cyclic amines and carbonyl-containing rings, alongside reactive substitutions and destructive edits; access to recognizable molecular families is established, while reliable discrimination among useful, chemically credible alternatives remains open. The unused pool members have no scores, so these runs cannot identify which rejected alternatives would have been better. Matched Parent replicas and same-pool comparisons with mean-only and generation-order selection are needed to isolate score benefit, efficiency, and uncertainty's contribution.
finding_summary.results: The two additional runs reproduce posterior selection and feedback. All 2,900 selected offspring maximize their reconstructed correlated function draws, uncertainty changes 2,693 choices (92.86%) compared with choosing the highest posterior mean, and all 2,800 eligible predictions on the same molecules change after accepted feedback. All 290 fits use only earlier accepted observations. Mean final-best score across the five objectives is 0.558863 in the first additional run and 0.526723 in the second, compared with 0.547535 in the original run of this selector. Across all three seeds, mean score is 0.544374 with population standard deviation 0.013310. The intended offspring-efficiency improvement does not appear: only 371 of 2,900 new offspring beat their best generating parent (12.79%), and their mean child-minus-parent score is -0.100465. The original direct-submission Parent's single-seed references are 13.86% and -0.084154. Across all three selector runs, 565 of 4,350 offspring beat their best parent (12.99%). The original paired screening-score gain of 0.055880 remains a one-seed comparison because matched additional runs of the direct-submission Parent are unavailable.

molecular.headline: Aromatic amides, cyclic amines and dicarbonyl heterocycles are abundant, but reactive halogen and peroxide substitutions persist.
molecular.overall_character: Every task has 600 observed molecules across seeds 1 and 2, including 580 optimizer proposals. Ring_closure_rate ranges from 0.9724 to 0.9966 and aromatic_atom_rate from 0.969 to 0.9897, supporting a predominantly ring-rich aromatic repertoire. These counters measure SMILES-text presence, not ring counts or fractions of aromatic atoms. The molecules include benzofused nitrogen heterocycles with aryl amides, bridged lactams, carbonyl-rich fused heteroaromatics, saturated cyclic aminals, macrocyclic nitrogen/carbonyl systems and fluorinated aryl primary amines. Thus useful rings, amines, carbonyls and heteroaromatic chemistry are demonstrably available. Mean SMILES lengths range from 45.0 to 85.3 and the maximum reaches 248; moderately sized leaders coexist with bulky assembled structures and occasional tiny fragments. Charged_rate is 0.0 throughout, which does not mean that neutral SMILES lack protonatable amines. Stereocentre_rate is also 0.0 despite several asymmetric saturated centres, ring junctions and constrained frameworks. The main chemical-quality issue is the persistence of nitrogen-halogen, oxygen-halogen and peroxide functionality, including among high-scoring structures. Some leading molecules are much more conventional, especially the primary-amine-bearing fluorinated aryl dicarbonyl family and ordinary carbon-linked cyclic amines. Synthetic plausibility is therefore mixed, and drug-likeness moderate overall. Core diversity is greater across runs than within their concentrated upper families; numerous local ring and substituent variants should not be mistaken for uniformly broad useful chemistry. The supplied parent_trajectories are seed 0 of n-fc2c108a5253 itself. Comparisons below describe those different runs and do not judge algorithm activation. Missing chemistry denotes gaps in the observed output, not established benefits for unobserved replacements.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 2 favours moderately sized benzofused unsaturated nitrogen-nitrogen rings bearing a carboxanilide, methoxy and methyl groups. The leading carboxanilide nitrogen is fluorinated, and other variants halogenate the ring nitrogen or add bromomethyl/chloromethyl groups. Seed 1 instead produces bridged or spiro-like lactam/imine frameworks containing an aromatic nitrogen ring and vinyl ether or vinyl sulfide decoration; some introduce sulfur-nitrogen bridges. Ring_closure_rate is 0.9724, aromatic_atom_rate 0.9707 and halogen_rate 0.8224. Recognizable amide and heterocycle chemistry is retained, but neither the N-fluoro amides nor all of the bridged sulfur variants are routine medicinal substitutions. Prior seed 0 reached 0.4463521672202675 with a bridged aromatic nitrogen/oxygen system bearing an aryl-containing ketone side chain. The new high families change core chemistry but remain below that observed best.
liabilities: N-fluoro amides, N-halogenated hydrazine-like rings and halomethyl substituents introduce reactive functionality into the high tail.
Nitrogen-nitrogen, sulfur-nitrogen and oxime-ether-like linkages add stability or configurational questions to already constrained structures.
Tiny late fragments discard the useful molecule rather than providing a coherent small analogue; bridged stereochemistry remains unspecified.
missing_features: Stable local alternatives to N-fluoro amides, ring-nitrogen halogenation and sulfur-nitrogen bridges are incompletely represented in the leading series, although a more conventional bridged lactam already reaches the upper neighbourhood.
Broader independent cores preserving the useful aromatic and carbonyl relationships are not established beyond the concentrated fused-nitrogen and bridged-lactam families.
Explicit configuration at asymmetric bridged centres and credible core-preserving contractions are absent from parts of the output.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial methoxyindole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145. The N-fluoro carboxanilide on the benzofused hydrazine-like ring reaches 0.4163503402962837, while the vinyl-sulfide, sulfur-nitrogen-bridged lactam/imine reaches 0.4126819838532174. A related vinyl-ether bridged lactam without that sulfur bridge scores 0.4005670758913022, showing a relatively conventional alternative in the same broad upper range. Adding chlorine or fluorine to the hydrazine-ring nitrogen gives 0.40314990987966176; changing the ring nitrogen pair to an oxygen/nitrogen connection gives 0.36286362320121707. A related imidamide-containing fused ring scores 0.40497388700123543. These observations favour coherent aromatic/polar cyclic arrangements over indiscriminate halogen addition. Ethene, methane, molecular fluorine and small sulfur or imine fragments appear at 0.0, and the seed-2 trajectory ends with ethene at 0.0. The useful cores are therefore not consistently preserved in all emissions.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-1 molecules join carbonyl-containing oxygen/nitrogen heteroaromatic ring systems through an amino linkage. They are heavily decorated with halogens, short ring bridges and, often, oxygen-oxygen-halogen chains. Several also carry an O-cyanate substituent, which is chemically different from a carbon-bound nitrile. Seed 2 develops a related but distinct family of coupled and bridged nitrogen dicarbonyl heterocycles with N-halogenation and halomethyl substitution. Ring_closure_rate and aromatic_atom_rate are both 0.9862; halogen_rate is 0.9552. Mean_smiles_length 85.3 and max_smiles_length 248 show a substantial bulky-assembly tail, although the supplied leaders are more compact than the most extended proposals. The prior seed-0 best, 0.6004556752278376, was a much more extensively assembled nitrogen/carbonyl heteroaromatic structure with conjugated appendages. The new upper structures are more compact connected heterocycles but introduce pronounced reactive-group liabilities.
liabilities: Oxygen-oxygen-halogen chains, oxygen-halogen bonds and O-cyanate groups make the leading chemistry substantially more reactive than an ordinary halogenated heteroaryl series.
Seed-2 late structures repeatedly carry nitrogen-fluorine or nitrogen-chlorine bonds, adding a separate stability concern.
Short bridges across aromatic frameworks and very large connected assemblies create geometric and synthetic demands that the score alone does not resolve.
missing_features: Chemically robust substituents that preserve the useful heteroaromatic arrangement are underrepresented relative to peroxide and heteroatom-halogen variants. The fluoromethyl analogue demonstrates that a less reactive alternative can retain a similar score.
Independent stable scaffold and linker alternatives are incompletely represented within the leading coupled-heterocycle families.
Reliable control of short ring bridges and avoidance of unnecessary multi-core concatenation are missing from parts of the broader output.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading amino-linked heterocycle with an oxygen-oxygen-chlorine substituent scores 0.6324703199409752. A closely related aza-ring version scores 0.6300605077662029, whereas replacing its oxygen-oxygen-chlorine group with fluoromethyl gives 0.6293992623616929. Chlorinated and brominated oxygen-containing side-chain alternatives also score 0.6293992623616929. Thus a nearly comparable upper value is observed with an ordinary carbon-bound fluorine substituent; the peroxide/oxygen-halogen motif is not demonstrably essential. A less bridged analogue scores 0.6309644029285534. The initial dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.548381482770623, and tiny chlorine, fluoromethane, enol-ether or cyanogen-halide fragments occupy the 0.5 floor. Late seed-2 nitrogen-halogen-rich dicarbonyl assemblies remain around 0.6058710298363812 and 0.6012872454997692. The gradient supports a specific connected heteroaromatic/carbonyl arrangement over isolated fragments or arbitrary size, while being relatively insensitive to some chemically consequential peripheral substitutions.

per_task.generated_character: The best seed-2 molecules combine halogenated aromatic rings with a saturated imidazolidine-type aminal ring, secondary or tertiary amines, and short aminoalkyl or enamine-containing connections to another substituted aromatic group. The leading central aminal carbon also bears an amino substituent. These are moderately large, recognizable amine-rich medicinal architectures, although aminal stability and some reactive substitutions remain concerns. Seed 1 reaches a different, more bridged amine/aryl family. Ring_closure_rate is 0.9828, aromatic_atom_rate 0.9724, halogen_rate 0.9828 and mean_smiles_length 58.7. Formal charge markers are absent, but accessible basic centres are abundant in the leading SMILES. The prior seed-0 leader scored 0.9908331648929692 and used a more rigid spiro saturated-amine framework between halogenated and thiol-substituted aromatic groups. Both old and new upper families clearly contain cyclic amines and substantial aromatic surface.
liabilities: Amino-substituted aminal centres, enamine functionality and multiple basic nitrogens require stability and physicochemical scrutiny beyond their high scores.
Chloromethyl, bromomethyl and thiol-containing side chains occur among near-leading variants.
The structures combine substantial aromatic/halogen content with basic centres, and some late variants disturb the aromatic or amine environment instead of preserving a coherent analogue.
missing_features: No absence of basic cyclic amines is supported; the missing coverage is stable, well-defined alternatives to the aminoaminal/enamine architecture that preserve its useful amine and aromatic relationships.
Control of nitrogen acylation, aromaticity and linker attachment is inconsistent, with some local changes losing much of the observed score.
Defined stereochemistry at the substituted aminoalkyl and aminal centres is missing; the trajectory does not establish a preferred configuration.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The amino-substituted imidazolidine with a carbon-linked secondary amine reaches 0.9914038363125457. The otherwise related example without that central amino substituent scores 0.9725868595115974. The enamine-connected counterpart scores 0.981088217863691, and its N-formyl analogue scores 0.48797702544581545, supporting a role for the local electronic state of the ring nitrogen. A halomethyl-substituted relative remains high at 0.989167131859766, whereas dearomatizing its terminal halogenated ring in a related family gives 0.08210159005746291. Removing the second aryl-containing amine side chain and retaining a hydroxylamine-like fragment yields 0.011495655106721757. Simple halogenated benzenes score 0.001421581552029289 and 0.0021330149885975206, while the acylated amino-acid starting-family derivative scores 0.000719339566735797. The visible preference is for the connected amine/aryl arrangement, not aromatic surface, amine count or halogenation alone.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 1 favours aryl-substituted bridged or fused nitrogen rings carrying multiple carbonyls, with an ethoxy benzofuran-like region and an N-fluoro centre in its leading structures. Seed 2 instead develops quinoline-linked macrocyclic nitrogen/carbonyl systems containing tertiary amines, amide-like carbonyls, and hydroxyl, methyl or thiol substitutions. These molecules range from medium-sized macrocycles to bulkier fused systems and have recognizable synthetic building blocks, although their full ring topology and some substitutions are demanding. Ring_closure_rate is 0.9966, aromatic_atom_rate 0.9897 and mean_smiles_length 56.6. The prior seed-0 best, 0.22405709718343647, was another nitrogen/carbonyl ring system combining aromatic and saturated regions. The new leaders change ring layout but remain in a similar chemical class and below that score.
liabilities: The leading seed-1 structures contain nitrogen-fluorine bonds, whereas a near-leading seed-2 macrocycle demonstrates a conventional alternative without that functionality.
Multiple carbonyls, tertiary amines and constrained ring systems create conformational and synthetic complexity; thiol-containing analogues add oxidation concerns.
Small cyclic peroxide fragments and overgrown multi-aryl variants occur at lower scores, showing that ring presence alone is not sufficient chemical organization.
missing_features: A broader set of stable cores that retain the useful macrocyclic or bridged nitrogen/carbonyl arrangement is not established beyond closely related upper families.
Coherent simplification and linker changes are incompletely explored: useful medium-sized macrocycles exist, but both fragmentation and further core duplication can lose the favourable arrangement.
Defined configuration at bridged saturated centres and adequate specification of constrained-ring geometry are missing.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial diaryl dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.1678386594791329. The N-fluoro bridged carbonyl structure reaches 0.2133697489012744, while the more conventionally bonded hydroxyquinoline-linked macrocycle scores 0.21037674112349405 and a related azaaryl/carbonyl macrocycle scores 0.20917089553667287. Hydroxyl-, methyl- and thiol-containing relatives share 0.20736246951923798, so those particular peripheral changes do not distinguish their recorded scores. Phenol alone scores 0.06793662204867576, the small aryl amide acid scores 0.07504633196017493, and ethane and a small cyclic peroxide score 0.012461119656980673 and 0.0239774717598468. A late structure adding a second quinoline-containing region scores only 0.1754730092490373. The apparent preference is for organized aromatic/nitrogen/carbonyl relationships and suitable ring size, not maximal molecular growth or N-fluorination as a universal requirement.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-1 family is a moderately sized, fluorinated aryl primary-amine series attached to a bicyclic nitrogen dicarbonyl heterocycle. The best molecule carries aminomethyl, aryl fluorine and fluoromethyl groups with ordinary carbon-bound fluorination; its core nitrogens are alkylated rather than directly fluorinated. Other high relatives use aminoethyl groups, fused small carbocycles or N-fluorination. This leading chemistry is more recognizable and plausibly makeable than the much larger linked dicarbonyl assemblies in the low tail. Seed 2 reaches a different fused heteroaromatic family with small fluorinated carbocycles, hydroxyl and thiomethyl groups. Ring_closure_rate is 0.9724, aromatic_atom_rate 0.969, halogen_rate 0.781 and mean_smiles_length 56.5. The prior seed-0 best, 0.4759777345546235, used an acylated nitrogen-rich fluorinated heterocycle with an unsaturated oxygen ring. The new highest family brings a clear primary-amine/aryl/dicarbonyl arrangement into the upper output.
liabilities: Direct nitrogen-fluorine bonds occur in several high relatives even though the leading molecule demonstrates ordinary carbon-bound fluorination and N-alkylation.
Other variants contain strained small unsaturated carbocycles, thiols or thiomethyl groups; their stability and stereochemical accessibility are not established.

Large duplicated or fused dicarbonyl assemblies produce substantial bulk with extremely poor recorded scores, indicating a need for coherent size and core organization rather than further concatenation.
missing_features: The useful primary amine is present in the leading family, but stable alternative cores and linkers preserving its placement relative to the aryl dicarbonyl system remain incompletely represented.
Consistent retention of the favourable local amino group is missing in some substitutions and in the alternative fused heteroaromatic trajectory.
Stereochemically specified small-ring variants are absent where configuration becomes relevant; the leading acyclic side-chain example itself does not require an assigned tetrahedral stereocentre.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The aminomethyl, fluoromethyl-substituted aryl dicarbonyl leader scores 0.5845583988949146. Replacing a peripheral fluoromethyl group with chlorine in the otherwise corresponding structure gives 0.5064928497454653. An aminoethyl analogue scores 0.5180292619150341; the full trajectory shows its closely matched terminal-amine-to-fluorine replacement at 0.0007365197806377691, supporting the importance of that local primary-amine functionality in this family. N-fluorinated aminoethyl relatives score 0.5652209810580261 and 0.5615749101173619, below the conventionally N-alkylated leader. Very large linked dicarbonyl molecules score 1.6758614448245604e-53 and 5.4391203474237023e-42. Seed 2 reaches 0.4071395189354175 with a small fluorinated carbocycle attached to its fused aromatic core, but ends at 0.0038179150668162477 after losing that substituent and changing nearby sulfur decoration. The gradient supports compact, correctly placed amine/aryl/carbonyl relationships; neither total fluorination nor accumulating more copies of the core is a sufficient rule.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited upper families contain N-fluoro amides and amines, oxygen-oxygen-halogen chains, oxygen-halogen bonds and O-cyanate substituents. Yet a fluoromethyl alternative scores 0.6293992623616929 near its peroxide-bearing relative at 0.6300605077662029, a conventional macrocycle scores 0.21037674112349405 near an N-fluorinated leader, and an ordinarily N-alkylated aryl primary amine leads another family at 0.5845583988949146. The data show usable conventional chemistry alongside reactive edits.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently prefer chemically robust local alternatives over reactive heteroatom-halogen and peroxide substitutions.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make stable functional-group replacements available while preserving the useful core and polar-group relationships. Treat carbon-bound halogens, nitrogen-halogen bonds and oxygen/peroxide-halogen chains as distinct chemistry, and use accepted molecular feedback to compare coherent alternatives instead of treating all halogen substitutions alike.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A connected cyclic-aminal/amine structure scores 0.9914038363125457, whereas deleting its second aryl-containing amine region gives 0.011495655106721757. In a related family, nitrogen formylation changes a 0.981088217863691 structure to one scoring 0.48797702544581545. The fluorinated aryl primary-amine family also shows a sharp loss when an aminoethyl terminus is replaced by fluorine. These observations establish local arrangement, not merely nitrogen or halogen abundance, as useful visible chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful amine and carbonyl attachment context is not reliably preserved during local substitution, acylation or linker changes.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve and deliberately vary the spacing, attachment and electronic environment of amines, aromatic groups and carbonyls. Distinguish free or cyclic amines from acylated, oxygen-linked or sulfur-linked nitrogen so feedback can assess chemically meaningful local changes.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Tiny ethene, methane and halogen fragments occupy zero or floor-score tails, while large duplicated dicarbonyl assemblies score 1.6758614448245604e-53 and 5.4391203474237023e-42. A late macrocycle acquiring an additional quinoline region scores 0.1754730092490373, below simpler relatives near 0.21037674112349405. Conversely, some useful molecules are themselves moderately large and cyclic, so the evidence does not support a universal size minimum or maximum.
transferable_gaps.gap: Size changes can discard useful cores or duplicate them into bulky assemblies instead of producing coherent analogues.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide core-preserving growth, contraction and linker moves that maintain complete functional groups. Let accepted observations determine useful size locally while maintaining alternatives to both fragmentation and repeated assembly of the same core.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0. The cited molecules include asymmetric aminoalkyl centres, substituted aminal carbons, bridged lactams and fluorinated small carbocycles. Such structures can have configurational alternatives even though all supplied strings omit stereocentre annotations. Short bridges and constrained rings also need more than a valid ring-closure string to define plausible geometry.
transferable_gaps.gap: Explicit stereochemistry and controlled geometric interpretation are missing from asymmetric cyclic and bridged structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent relevant stereochemical and geometric alternatives when changing saturated centres, constrained alkenes or ring junctions. Preserve chemically credible connectivity and let accepted feedback determine useful configurations; their present absence does not establish a score benefit for any one choice.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The high tails repeatedly revisit benzofused aryl amides or bridged lactams, coupled carbonyl heteroaromatics, imidazolidine-type amine architectures, quinoline-linked macrocycles and aryl primary-amine dicarbonyl systems. Different seeds reach distinct cores, so scaffold change is possible, but many leading examples differ only by local halogen, heteroatom or ring edits and some receive identical scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: Coverage of independent useful chemical cores remains narrower than the number of local analogues and peripheral edits suggests.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Maintain several chemically distinct accepted core families and support scaffold replacements that preserve useful donor, acceptor, amine and aromatic relationships. Evaluate coverage through credible core chemistry and attachment geometry alongside molecular identity, rather than relying on a new substituent or ring closure alone.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

activation_observables.measurement: Audit every fit's ordered training identities and scores against previously accepted same-process observations, including initial observations and discarded survivors, with zero unscored pool members or future labels. The Parent has no posterior fit. After each nonterminal feedback batch, compare the next fit's mean and standard deviation on the identical previously emitted molecules against their logged pre-feedback predictions; report fit-count, archive growth and nonzero fixed-probe prediction displacement. Terminal feedback without a later suggestion is excluded from update opportunities. Reconstruct the posterior from the declared fingerprints, kernel, normalization, noise and recorded jitter.
activation_observables.name: accepted_only_fingerprint_posterior_updates

activation_observables.measurement: For every nonfallback batch position, reconstruct its joint Gaussian function vector from the logged normal vector and conditional posterior, and verify that the emitted candidate is the maximum over that position's available pool mask. Report its sampled value minus the available-pool sampled-value mean, its sample-rank enrichment relative to uniform pool selection, and the proportion of positions with positive margins. The direct-submission Parent has no within-pool selection, corresponding to zero selection enrichment. Log the fraction of emitted identities outside the same pool's first announced-batch-size generation-order candidates, so the selection change is observed on identical generated alternatives rather than inferred from different search trajectories.
activation_observables.name: joint_posterior_draw_selection_enrichment

activation_observables.measurement: Using each position's identical available candidate mask, compare the posterior-sample argmax with the posterior-mean argmax, breaking ties by pool generation order. Report disagreement counts and fractions, pool posterior-standard-deviation ranges, and nonzero posterior off-diagonal covariance. A positive disagreement count demonstrates that posterior uncertainty affected an emitted choice beyond deterministic prediction ranking; the Parent reference is zero such choices. Report this per task and pooled, separately from numerical fallbacks and exact kernel-equivalent fingerprint ties.
activation_observables.name: posterior_uncertainty_changes_offspring_choices

activation_observables.measurement: Join every accepted emitted offspring to its logged generating parents and its pre-feedback posterior version. Compare its strict best-parent-beating fraction and mean child-minus-best-parent score with the Parent's 201/1450 and -0.0841535792773 references, per task and pooled on the supplied paired execution panel. Also report chronological posterior-mean squared error relative to the same fit's archive-mean predictor and per-batch predicted-versus-observed rank association. These measure predictive transfer and proposal efficiency after selection; unselected pool members remain unlabelled and provide no claimed oracle counterfactual.
activation_observables.name: selected_offspring_parent_beating_rate

applicability_conditions: Applies to task-local scalar molecular maximization when accepted scores have learnable local structure in the declared fingerprint similarity and graph operators can cheaply produce a pool larger than the announced oracle batch.

The observed limitation is supported by the supplied Parent's single screening seed. A reliable final-score effect requires the protocol's own comparable evaluations; no cross-seed reliability or causal advantage is already established.
The Gaussian process represents only finite accepted observations from the current objective; rejected proposals, unselected pool members and observations from other tasks cannot train it.

The posterior draws are exact for the declared fixed kernel, normalization and noise model, not a claim that molecular objectives follow that prior or that posterior uncertainty is calibrated. Sparse initial evidence and fingerprint collisions can limit selection quality.

Generation, novelty checks and bounded retries must still yield complete valid batches. Numerical fallback is bounded and visible, and fallback output does not count as posterior-selection activation.
No settled Mechanism Cluster or earlier sibling Child exists in the supplied lineage evidence, so this is a first test rather than a revisit.

finding_summary.headline: Posterior selection reproduces across seeds, but offspring yield stays below the historical parent-beating rate
finding_summary.insights: The experiment now separates reliable selector execution from the hoped-for improvement in offspring yield. The new runs' posterior means contain useful predictive information on the selected molecules: pooled prediction MSE is 0.017182 versus 0.036613 for the same-fit archive mean, with average within-batch rank correlation 0.412. The remaining question is how to turn predictive information into more productive evaluations relative to already strong parents. Prediction quality is also uneven: on sitagliptin_mpo it is worse than the archive-mean predictor in two of three seeds, and that objective has the largest final-score variation. The chemistry assessment shows ample aromatic amides, cyclic amines and carbonyl-containing rings, alongside reactive substitutions and destructive edits; access to recognizable molecular families is established, while reliable discrimination among useful, chemically credible alternatives remains open. The unused pool members have no scores, so these runs cannot identify which rejected alternatives would have been better. Matched Parent replicas and same-pool comparisons with mean-only and generation-order selection are needed to isolate score benefit, efficiency, and uncertainty's contribution.

molecular_assessment.headline: Ring-rich aromatic series and spiro diamines coexist with oversized imide assemblies, reactive bonds, and unassigned stereochemistry.
molecular_assessment.overall_character: Read the digest and the complete supplied child and Parent trajectories for every listed objective; the digest reports no tasks without trajectories. Each child trajectory contains 300 observed molecules, including 290 optimizer proposals, on seed 0. The output has abundant rings, aromatic groups, carbonyls, and nitrogen functionality. Distinct trajectories develop compact annulated heterocycles, large repeated imide-containing assemblies, saturated spiro diamines, large nitrogen-containing ring closures, or fluorinated pyrroles with oxygen-containing rings. This supports moderate diversity across the complete output, although the high-scoring end of each trajectory is a close analogue series. Apparent makeability is mixed: ordinary aryl groups, amines, ketones, and amides coexist with unusual ring fusions, oxygen-halogen bonds, peroxides, and cyclic cumulenes. The chemistry-quality judgements describe structures, not a synthesis calculation or measured drug properties. All task digests have stereocentre_rate 0.0 and charged_rate 0.0. These indicate no explicit stereochemical or charge annotations in the proposals; they do not mean that the molecules lack stereogenic centres or protonatable amines, and they reveal nothing about any downstream protonation treatment. The quoted ring and aromatic rates are molecule-level SMILES-text incidences, not ring counts or fractions of atoms perceived as aromatic. Parent comparisons below describe observed chemical differences and recorded scores only; they do not establish a causal mechanism or infer hidden objective definitions.

per_task.generated_character: The upper end consists of relatively compact ethyl/methyl-substituted, annulated nitrogen/oxygen polycycles carrying an aryl or heteroaryl carbonyl side arm. The best cited structure, evaluation 150, is a polycyclic N/O core bearing a fluoropyridylmethyl ketone; related upper-end structures contain ketones, a thioester, or an N-S-containing ring. Mean SMILES length is 43.6, with ring_closure_rate and aromatic_atom_rate both 0.9759 and halogen_rate 0.9621. The Parent upper end instead contains less entangled indole/benzimidazole-like heteroaromatic carboxanilides with alkoxy/alkyl substitution. The child retains aromatic and carbonyl chemistry while moving toward more highly connected ring systems and ketone linkers. These are substantial small-molecule frameworks, but the bridged/annulated connectivity gives less obvious synthetic routes than the Parent carboxamide series.
liabilities: Unusual annulated/bridged N/O connectivity and the N-S ring variants make synthetic accessibility uncertain from the structures alone.
The cited thioester is a potentially reactive acyl linkage; this is a chemical liability, not evidence that every carbonyl-containing proposal is unsuitable.
Very small fragments and repeated-core products occur even late in the trajectory, and nonplanar variants have no assigned stereochemistry.
missing_features: The low-scoring fragments and truncated polycycle lack the connected fluorinated aromatic arm plus carbonyl-bearing core found in the upper-end series.

The cited upper end supplies this arrangement mainly through closely related, intricate ring systems. Chemically ordinary alternative frameworks preserving the same arrangement are poorly represented there; the observations do not identify an additional mandatory target-specific group.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial indole carboxanilide at evaluation 9 scores 0.3051048083696145; the Parent maximum is 0.4145039882261785 and the child maximum is 0.4463521672202675 at evaluation 150. The child upper end preserves a compact combination of an aromatic polycycle, a carbonyl, and a fluorinated aryl/azaaryl arm. Evaluation 297, which has a smaller propionyl substituent instead of the fluorinated heteroaryl arm, scores 0.07743009616575633. The isolated F and N proposals score 0.0, while the large repeated polycyclic assembly at evaluation 51 scores 7.948399140387414e-20. Thus both deletion of the combined structural context and gross multiplication of it accompany poor scores. This supports a local preference for a compact linked arrangement, not a general rule that more rings, nitrogen, or molecular size always helps. The final proposal scores 0.3391993439193198, below the best observed structure; it should not be treated as the chemical endpoint of a monotonic trajectory.

per_task.generated_character: This trajectory produces the largest textual structures: mean SMILES length 112.5 and maximum 229, with ring_closure_rate and aromatic_atom_rate both 0.9931. The upper end is dominated by densely substituted aryl/azaaryl assemblies containing repeated N-rich, carbonyl-bearing heterocycles, N-methyl and N-vinyl groups, formamides, and acetyl or unsaturated acyl substituents. Some nitrogen/carbonyl rings are expanded beyond the familiar small fused imide motif of the initial material. The best cited molecule at evaluation 275 has repeated heterocyclic dione units joined through a substituted diarylamine arrangement, together with a brominated azaaryl group and a vinyl ketone. The Parent also reaches conjugated multiaryl imide chemistry, but the child upper end more prominently repeats bulky heterocyclic units. These are complex heteroatom-rich assemblies with substantially less ordinary medicinal-chemistry size and connectivity than the compact starting fragments.
liabilities: Repeated heterocycles and heavily substituted aryl connections create substantial size, functional-group density, and synthetic complexity; the SMILES lengths are text measurements, not molecular-weight estimates.
Vinyl ketones and alkynyl ketones in cited upper-end structures are electrophilic motifs; N-vinyl and expanded carbonyl-rich heterocyclic arrangements also warrant chemical stability assessment.
The cited lower end includes a peroxide and a carbamoyl chloride, showing access to chemically reactive connectivity as well as ordinary amide-like groups.
missing_features: The low-end fragments lack the connected combination of aromatic surfaces and multiple nitrogen/carbonyl functions carried by the higher-scoring assemblies.

The upper-end examples do not show compact, non-repeated alternatives presenting comparable functional relationships. That is a chemical coverage gap; the visible scores do not demonstrate that compactness is an objective requirement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused heterocyclic dione at evaluation 7 scores 0.548381482770623. The Parent maximum is 0.5988706970837679 and the child maximum is 0.6004556752278376 at evaluation 275. In contrast, methylamine scores 0.5, the vinyl-substituted carbamoyl chloride at evaluation 143 scores 0.500440955992592, and the small azaaryl imine at evaluation 108 scores 0.5048505159185113. The observed gradient favours connected aromatic/heteroaromatic, nitrogen/carbonyl-rich assemblies over these small fragments. It does not show a corresponding reward for synthetic simplicity: an even more elaborated repeated-unit molecule at evaluation 288 still scores 0.598530640326306. The final molecule remains in the repeated heterocyclic series and scores 0.5993640699523053. The modest score separation among elaborate upper-end molecules does not establish which individual group is essential or that duplication itself is causally beneficial.

per_task.generated_character: The upper end is a recognisable basic-amine series: saturated spirocyclic diamines carrying a brominated/chlorinated aryl substituent and a benzylic aryl-thiol arm. Several analogues also contain phenol, fluoroalkyl, or additional amine substitution. The best structure at evaluation 300 combines a secondary ring amine with a substituted tertiary ring amine; the neutral SMILES therefore does not imply a lack of basic centres. Mean SMILES length is 63.2, ring_closure_rate and aromatic_atom_rate are both 0.9897, and halogen_rate is 0.9966. The Parent upper end includes aryl/azaaryl systems with pendant cyclic amines and, in its maximum-scoring example, an amino-acid-like side chain. The child upper end instead concentrates these aryl and amine elements around spiro connectivity and largely removes the carboxyl group. The ordinary amine and aryl bonds are synthetically credible, although substitution pattern, spiro construction, and the reactive analogues make the series mixed in practical plausibility.
liabilities: Some highly scored analogues contain aryl O-Cl or aliphatic O-F bonds, which are chemically distinct from ordinary stable carbon-halogen substitution.
The aryl thiol creates oxidation/reactivity concerns, and the combination of halogenated aromatic surfaces and basic amines does not by itself establish solubility or selectivity.
Several nonplanar stereogenic environments remain unspecified despite the strong dependence of molecular shape on their configuration.
missing_features: The low-scoring isolated aryl fragment lacks the saturated nonamidic amine framework and its connection to the second aromatic arm. The upper-end molecules already contain this combination; a general claim that the generator cannot make basic ring amines would be wrong.

The spiro and benzylic structures have no explicit stereochemical assignments, and their ionisation states are only implicit in neutral SMILES. These are untested chemical-state dimensions, not demonstrated missing requirements for a higher score.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The Parent maximum is 0.9050950749844976; the child maximum is 0.9908331648929692 at evaluation 300. The isolated bromochlorodimethylbenzene-like fragment at evaluation 231 scores 0.002450271387431188, and the bulky initial quinoline/amide/hydroxamate structure at evaluation 6 scores 0.0003786988088202195. The latter already contains a cyclic amine, so a basic centre alone is insufficient. The visible separation instead associates the combined saturated amine-ring geometry and attached aromatic groups with higher scores. Phenol is not an invariant upper-end requirement: evaluation 294 carries it and scores 0.9673692982895326, whereas the best cited molecule lacks it, although ring connectivity also differs so this is not a matched deletion experiment. Aryl hypochlorite-containing evaluation 289 scores 0.9883741581042836 and the O-F-containing evaluation 278 scores 0.9720734433524977. High reported scores therefore coexist with chemically labile motifs and should not be read as evidence of compound stability.

per_task.generated_character: The high-scoring family combines an alkyl-substituted pyridyl group with a benzofused carbonyl-containing heterocycle and a large nitrogen-containing ring closure. The ring system includes N-methyl amine or amide/urea-like variants, with occasional alcohol, ether, or sulfur substitution. These are medium-to-large, partly saturated polycyclic frameworks rather than aromatic fragments alone. Mean SMILES length is 54.4, ring_closure_rate 0.9897, aromatic_atom_rate 0.9862, and halogen_rate 0.1207; the cited upper end is not a heavily halogenated family. The Parent upper end instead centres on diaryl, partly saturated nitrogen/carbonyl ring systems with alkoxy/alkyl substituents. The child shifts toward alkylpyridyl substitution and a benzofused lactam-like aromatic system. The functional groups are recognisable, but the large ring closures and unusual N-acyl connectivity make a practical synthetic route less evident than the mere presence of ordinary amines and carbonyls might suggest.
liabilities: Large ring closures and N-acyl lactam/urea-like connectivity raise conformational and synthetic questions that are not settled by the observed scores.
A cited low-scoring aromatic hydroperoxide demonstrates that the proposal set also includes reactive oxygen-oxygen connectivity.
Stereogenic saturated ring positions are not assigned; the output does not establish a particular stereoisomer or conformational preference.
missing_features: The low-scoring pyridyl and amide fragments lack the connected azaaryl, carbonyl-rich fused system, and nitrogen-containing ring arrangement seen together at the upper end.

The upper end has few alternative, synthetically simpler presentations of these functional relationships. Its close-series scores do not identify an unseen compulsory substituent or justify a task-specific pharmacophore prescription.

This supports sensitivity to the placement and linkage of existing functionality, not merely its presence. The isolated alkyl/alkoxy pyridine at evaluation 182 scores 0.10432570627183, the small amide at evaluation 80 scores 0.025605696979529788, and S scores 0.0. The high-score combination is thus missing from each small fragment. The hydroxylated near-best structure at evaluation 296 scores 0.2183193397487884, providing no support for a blanket claim that adding polarity helps. The final proposal remains in the alkyl-azaaryl/polycyclic series at 0.2089023722455138.

per_task.generated_character: The upper end is a compact fluorinated N-methylpyrrole series bearing an N-formylated urea with an iminomethyl substituent, together with an unsaturated oxygen-containing ring or a bridged oxygen-containing ring system. The best cited molecule at evaluation 263 has a difluorinated pyrrole and a partly saturated oxygen-containing diene ring. Other high scorers contain strained-looking cyclic cumulenes or thiol-substituted bridged rings. Mean SMILES length is 46.0, ring_closure_rate 0.9793, aromatic_atom_rate 0.8862, halogen_rate 0.5897, and cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.1448. The Parent upper end is chemically different: methoxy/acetal-rich annulated N/O heterocycles, including fluorinated variants. The child replaces that family with more carbonyl/imine functionality and a pyrrole/oxygen-ring combination. Its ordinary functional groups are accompanied by unusual substitution and ring unsaturation, so apparent synthetic plausibility remains questionable.
liabilities: Cyclic cumulated double bonds are a geometric and stability concern; their occurrence among high-scoring structures does not demonstrate isolable, useful compounds.
The N-formylated urea/iminomethyl arrangement combines unusual acylation with potentially tautomeric or hydrolytically sensitive functionality; no stability measurement is supplied.
The bridged oxygen-containing and thiol-bearing analogues have unspecified stereochemistry, and repeated-core products can become chemically convoluted while scoring extremely poorly.
missing_features: Low-scoring fragments lack the complete fluorinated heteroaryl, urea/imine, and oxygen-ring combination, while enlarged products fail to retain the compact presentation associated with the upper end.

The cited upper-end family does not provide a broad set of stereochemically specified, chemically ordinary alternatives to its bridged and cumulene-containing variants. The best example itself has no cumulene, so the observations do not establish a need for that liability.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited upper-end output includes an aryl hypochlorite-bearing molecule scoring 0.9883741581042836, an O-F-bearing analogue scoring 0.9720734433524977, and a cyclic cumulene-containing molecule scoring 0.41549616525530514. A supplied proposal digest has cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.1448. Cited lower-end structures also contain peroxides and a carbamoyl chloride. Thus reactive connectivity is not confined to one score extreme, and molecular graph complexity does not establish stability.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently restrict local bonding and ring unsaturation to chemically stable, practically credible structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make chemically credible local bonding and ring geometry an objective-independent property of candidate construction, while retaining ordinary amines, carbonyls, heterocycles, and carbon-halogen substitution. Provide stable structural alternatives to labile oxygen-halogen linkages and implausible cyclic cumulenes; whether those alternatives improve the observed objective must remain a question for task-local feedback.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Cited isolated F, N, and S proposals score 0.0 in their respective observed trajectories, while intact compact ring/carbonyl/heteroaryl combinations reach 0.4463521672202675 or 0.4759777345546235. Repeated or crosslinked versions of those compact series can score 7.948399140387414e-20 or 3.378515532563205e-25. Conversely, a different observed series has large repeated heterocyclic assemblies near its upper score range, including 0.6004556752278376. These are within-trajectory contrasts, not comparable score scales or evidence for a universal preferred size.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve a useful combination of molecular fragments when changing size or connectivity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make controlled fragment-preserving replacement, addition, and deletion accessible so that changes need not alternate between losing the whole functional arrangement and duplicating much of a scaffold. Let accepted local scores determine which size and connectivity changes remain useful; the evidence does not support a universal small-molecule cutoff.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every supplied proposal digest has stereocentre_rate 0.0, although the cited molecules include substituted spiro diamines, benzylic centres, and bridged oxygen-containing rings. The structures therefore describe connectivity without resolving several chemically meaningful configurations. All charged_rate values are also 0.0, but the amine-rich examples show that this separate text observation must not be mistaken for absent basicity.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator leaves the stereochemistry of its nonplanar molecular output unspecified.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve and make accessible chemically valid stereochemical assignments when producing nonplanar ring systems and substituted saturated centres. The observed outputs justify a representation and coverage gap, not a claim that any particular stereoisomer or protonation state has already been shown to score better.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Each digest reports 300 unique molecules, yet its best_molecules excerpt is largely a close series: annulated carbonyl-bearing heterocycles, repeated heterocyclic diones, spiro diamines, large nitrogen-containing ring closures, or fluorinated pyrrole/oxygen-ring combinations. The complete trajectories do contain broader early and lower-scoring structures, so this is upper-end chemotype concentration rather than a total inability to generate diverse rings.
transferable_gaps.gap: The high-scoring output offers few distinct scaffold families for a given observed functional-group arrangement.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make alternative ring and linker frameworks available while preserving functional relationships that have support in accepted local observations. Seek new scaffold presentations through generic chemistry operations, with the current objective deciding their value; do not supply a named-objective template or assume that canonical uniqueness measures scaffold variety.

possible_failure_causes: The registered pooled parent-beating efficiency increase failed despite complete selector activation: 194 rather than 201 strict improvers, and a more negative mean child-minus-best-parent score. This is observed efficacy evidence, not a missing-execution diagnosis.

Predictive transfer was heterogeneous. On sitagliptin_mpo, posterior-mean MSE 0.0217476552541 exceeded archive-mean MSE 0.0166007117081 and mean within-batch Spearman correlation was only 0.147753396029. Fingerprint/kernel mismatch or excessive exploratory selection are possible explanations; this run does not distinguish them or assess posterior calibration.

Single-seed path dependence remains unresolved. The selector consumed a larger generated pool and changed subsequent populations and parent scores; the logged same-pool choice comparisons prove selection behavior but do not provide unselected oracle outcomes or a mean-only causal comparison.

The supplied molecular assessment identifies reactive bonding, repeated oversized motifs and unresolved stereochemistry among scored output. Better scalar scores therefore do not establish broader chemical usefulness, and chemically poor selected proposals remain a possible source of wasted evaluations.

End-to-end wall time increased substantially, with most of the increase recorded in deco_hop oracle evaluation. The experiment does not isolate the portion attributable to selected molecular complexity, evaluator variability, and selector computation.

approach.method_basis: The Parent is a genetic algorithm that breeds molecular graphs from a population of up to sixty-four scored molecules. It draws parents from three high-ranking score bands, makes connected-fragment crossovers and local atom or bond edits, and sends each valid, novel offspring directly for evaluation. Accepted scores immediately update a greedy survivor population, so useful offspring can become parents of the next batch. This feedback loop worked, but most evaluated offspring scored below their generating parents.
approach.novelty: Add posterior-sampling selection before offspring reach the oracle. The same graph operators first generate a fresh pool; a fingerprint Gaussian process learned only from this task's accepted scores draws plausible score functions, and each batch position takes a different sampled function's best available offspring. This concentrates evaluations on promising generated structures while allowing uncertainty to change the choices. The lineage has only its root so far: no sibling has tested learned offspring selection, and the supplied mechanism-cluster history is empty. The new mechanism changes which generated offspring are evaluated; its training archive and diagnostics support that single selection mechanism.

research_intent.falsifier: The selection mechanism is refuted if complete receipts show that fits use unaccepted, future or cross-task labels; emitted nonfallback choices fail to maximize their recorded joint posterior draws on the available pool; every batch bypasses the selector; or selection never changes any generation-order batch despite larger nondegenerate pools. The posterior-sampling component is refuted if complete evidence shows zero uncertainty-driven disagreement with the same-mask posterior-mean maximizer throughout nondegenerate pools, or if function values were sampled as independent candidate noises instead of from the declared joint conditional covariance. Feedback adaptation is refuted if accepted nonterminal score updates never change posterior predictions on the registered fixed probes despite new informative observations. Missing diagnostics make these claims inconclusive. If posterior selection and feedback activate but chronological prediction quality, parent-beating rate or final Top-1 do not improve, record failed predictive transfer or negative score evidence rather than retroactively calling the selector unexecuted.

research_intent.mechanism: Select oracle-bound offspring by maximizing independent joint posterior function draws from a task-local fingerprint Gaussian process over a fresh pool generated by the Parent's unchanged graph evolution operators.
research_intent.observed_bottleneck: The Parent n-4fa9546e559e achieved a screening macro mean of 0.491654854899 with valid graph evolution and all registered root observables active, but only 201 of 1450 accepted offspring strictly beat their best breeding parent (0.138620689655), and mean child-minus-best-parent score was -0.0841535792773. That mean was negative on every task. The actual summary and run log report successful complete execution with no external invalid or duplicate proposals; generation validity is therefore not the observed limitation. The limiting behavior is direct oracle submission of unselected graph offspring despite a large fraction of unproductive edits. These are single-seed observations, not a paired causal estimate of a filtering benefit.
